findings.what: the exit codes (0/1/2) are a contract scripts branch on and no document stated them. Measured, documented as a table, and pinned by a test that needs no root; verified it bites.

std::process::exit skips destructors, including FlashGuard's FATAL notice. Safe because the guard drops inside run_with — verified by observing FATAL precede main's error: line on an interrupted flash — but the argument was nowhere.

second pass: the doc's claim that FATAL, not the exit code, distinguishes a refusal from a half-written device was untested. Demonstrated both ways and pinned the root-free half. The test reaches only the no-guard path — stated in its doc after a mutation showed it — and a first cross-reference to the guard-exists case named the wrong test.

review_order_rationale: Dependency depth first: a file is reviewed only after everything it relies on, so a consumer can be judged against understood foundations. Within a tier the more destructive file comes first.

api_review.surface: rustdoc JSON: 8 structs, 6 enums, 1 trait, 1 type alias, 10 modules, 12 public fields, 26 public functions, plus 8 Events methods and the derived trait impls at default visibility. An earlier figure of '64 items' came from a filter that dropped default-visibility items and deduplicated names; it undercounted.
